findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the DC comment-diff (`outbound_comments._diff_comments`, injected codec at `outbound_comments.py:286`) as a consumer affected by redefining `WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound`, and add/name a DC comment-diff convergence test alongside `test_dc_cutover_converges`.
evidence: Plan: 'redefine `WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound` to the compare form `decode_inbound(to_wire(t))`'

Plan: 'the comment dedup that depends on it (`outbound_comments.py:48`) are preserved by routing every compare through the codec op' — asserts preservation but does not enumerate the DC comment-diff consumer or a proving test
outbound_comments.py:286 `codec = _resolve_codec(codec)`; _diff_comments builds its Jira-side comparison key through this codec
outbound_comments.py:106-116 _IdentityCodec docstring: 'Data Center's own codec (`WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound`) is already the identity — so falling back to identity here changes nothing'
findings.finding: Redefining WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound from identity to the rendering form decode_inbound(to_wire(t)) also changes the DC comment-diff dedup key, a consumer the plan does not enumerate. outbound_comments._diff_comments consumes the injected codec's normalize_outbound (outbound_comments.py _resolve_codec:123, used :286), and _IdentityCodec's docstring (outbound_comments.py:106-116) states DC's WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound being identity is precisely what keeps the DC comment-diff key on plain text today. The plan names only the description send/compare consumers (outbound_mapper.py:77, outbound_fields.py:564, inbound_differ.py:210) and asserts the codec law preserves comment dedup, but neither lists the DC comment-diff as an affected consumer nor names a test proving DC comment-diff still converges after the redefinition.
findings.location: 'DC' bullet under 'The live cutover' + Scope (adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py); Testing/AC (no DC comment-diff convergence test)
scenarios: A DC issue with mirrored comments is reconciled after the cutover; the comment dedup key is now computed over rendered wiki instead of the plain identity, so an already-mirrored comment could re-emit or a Jira-native comment edit could be swallowed if the law does not hold end-to-end for comment bodies as it does for descriptions.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `outbound_comments.py` (the `_diff_comments` codec consumer) to Scope for DC, and add a `test_dc_comment_diff_converges_after_render` proving an already-mirrored DC comment emits zero updates once `WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound` renders.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the outbound directionality guard (`_suppressed_by_inbound`) and the both-sides conflict scan (`_local_matches_baseline`) rich-codec-aware — normalize the RAW local description through the same codec op before comparing it to the decoded baseline — and add these sites to Scope, mirroring the local-normalization inbound_differ.py:208-212 already applies; otherwise a rendered baseline never matches raw Markdown and the body re-emits every pass, breaking origin-gating (AC5) and second-pass convergence (AC1/AC2).
evidence: The plan makes only the emit compare rich-aware: Scope lists 'outbound_field_diff.py (:273-293, :354-362) — make the EXISTING description compare rich-codec-aware'; it never lists the directionality guard.
outbound_field_diff.py:248-258 `_suppressed_by_inbound` and :277 call it with RAW `local_desc = ticket.get('description')`; :258 does `_text_matches(local_val, baseline.get(field))`.
The both-sides conflict scan at :359 uses `_local_matches_baseline` (:369-385) which also compares RAW `ticket.get('description')` against `baseline.get('description')`.

The baseline is decoded through the same `map_remote_to_local` at outbound_field_diff.py:197; DC's `_DCInbound.map_remote_to_local` (backend.py:126-129) is identity on a str, so the decoded baseline is the STORED RENDERED WIKI, not Markdown.

inbound_differ.py:208-212 already normalizes its local comparison copy through the codec op ('Normalize the local comparison copy identically or inbound clobbers the local wrapping') — the outbound guard needs the same and the plan omits it.

Plan step 3 asserts 'decode(baseline_wire) and the compare's decode(remote_wire) are the identical normalizer', but that holds only for the emit compare at :292 (which compares the codec-fitted local), NOT for the guard/conflict scan which compare raw local text.
findings.finding: Origin-gating and the both-sides conflict scan compare the RAW local description (Markdown) against the decoded baseline (rendered wiki for DC / adf_to_markdown for Cloud), so post-cutover they mismatch on every pass even with no rebar edit — breaking the 'exactly once' convergence and origin-gating the plan promises.
scenarios: DC: a synced ticket whose Markdown description renders to non-identical wiki (headings, bold, links); every reconcile pass sees raw markdown != decoded wiki baseline, so `_suppressed_by_inbound` returns False and a description update re-emits forever.

Cloud: a description with any construct where adf_to_markdown(markdown_to_adf(x)) != x on the decoded baseline vs raw local triggers perpetual re-emit and can spuriously trip the conflict alert when remote also diverged.
findings.suggested_fix: In `_suppressed_by_inbound` and `_local_matches_baseline`, for `description` compare `codec.normalize_outbound(local_desc)` (the same transform the emit compare fits) against the decoded baseline, not the raw local string; add outbound_field_diff.py :248-258 and :369-385 to the Scope list and add a test asserting a no-op DC/Cloud pass suppresses the description (0 outbound) when local==baseline under rendering.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate inbound_differ.py:212 (the remote-side adf.normalize_description(jira_val)) alongside :210 and specify whether it becomes codec-aware, confirming via find_referencing_symbols on adf.normalize_description that both compare halves stay the identical normalizer post-cutover.
evidence: Plan: 'the direct adf.normalize_description / adf.fit_text_to_adf_limit compare sites at outbound_fields.py:564 and inbound_differ.py:210 — paired so the send-fit and the compare-fit are the identical transform'

Code: inbound_differ.py:210 'local_val = adf.normalize_description(adf.fit_text_to_adf_limit(local_val))' and inbound_differ.py:212 'jira_val = adf.normalize_description(jira_val)' — the remote-side normalize in the same compare block, not enumerated
findings.finding: The Cloud compare-site inventory names outbound_fields.py:564 and inbound_differ.py:210 (both the LOCAL-side adf.normalize_description(adf.fit_text_to_adf_limit(local_val))), but omits inbound_differ.py:212, jira_val = adf.normalize_description(jira_val) — the REMOTE-side normalize within the same inbound compare, a distinct call to the same adf.normalize_description symbol being repointed.
findings.location: The live cutover → Cloud bullet: 'the direct adf.normalize_description / adf.fit_text_to_adf_limit compare sites at outbound_fields.py:564 and inbound_differ.py:210'; Scope: 'inbound_differ.py (:210)'
scenarios: inbound_differ.py:212 (jira_val = adf.normalize_description(jira_val)) stays on plain adf.normalize_description while :210's local side becomes markdown-codec-aware — the two sides of the inbound description compare use mismatched normalizers, re-emitting the body every pass and violating the plan's step-3 'normalizers must compose' invariant

findings.checklist_item: Reconcile the leaf's 'local-wins + outbound-field-conflict alert' concurrency policy with the parent's named 'three-way LWW' + '799/799-detected' AC4 — either realign the leaf to the parent's LWW/799-799 contract, or update the parent epic (re-staling its review) to adopt local-wins and restate AC4's verification.
evidence: Parent 708d Approach: 'concurrency is last-write-wins over a three-way state (baseline/local/remote)'
Parent 708d child responsibility: 'three-way LWW that always flags concurrent conflict'
Parent 708d AC4: 'always detected and flagged rather than silently overwritten; verified by the concurrent-conflict regression test over the corpus (the proven 799/799-detected invariant)'
Leaf: 'reuses the repo's settled concurrency policy (story a713: local-wins + a deduped outbound-field-conflict bridge alert … rather than inventing a new arbitration'
Leaf AC/testing names test_concurrent_conflict_alerts with no 799/799 corpus assertion; leaf title still reads 'LWW conflict safety' though body abandons LWW terminology
findings.finding: The leaf redefines the parent's named concurrency-arbitration deliverable: the parent epic specifies 'three-way LWW' (last-write-wins) and parent AC4 requires the 'proven 799/799-detected invariant', but the leaf replaces LWW with story-a713 'local-wins + a deduped outbound-field-conflict bridge alert' and its concurrency test (test_concurrent_conflict_alerts) does not carry the 799/799 assertion the parent AC names.
findings.location: Plan under review — 'Prior art' bullet 2 and 'Approach' step 4 / AC 'A concurrent both-sides body edit…'; parent 708d Approach + AC4

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the single writer and write-timing for the inline `rich_sha` (and reconcile it with 'compare never writes back'), and specify its retirement when a binding is deleted.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether the cutover flag supports a staged/canary rollout (e.g. subset of projects/bindings) or justify why a single per-client flip is acceptable given the one-time re-emit wave.

findings.finding: Rollout is described only as a binary per-client flag flip ('gated behind a single switch') with 'one revert' rollback. For a long-running reconciler that will re-emit every already-synced description once on cutover, there is no staged/canary rollout (e.g. by project or binding subset) described to bound the blast radius of the one-time re-emit wave.
findings.location: The live cutover — Rollback bullet; Approach step 1 ('re-emit exactly once')
scenarios: Flipping the flag on for a client with many bindings triggers a single mass re-emit pass across all descriptions at once.

"Cloud convergence: after the cutover, a converted ADF description posts once"

findings.finding: For a cutover that makes the rich codecs the DEFAULT live send path, the named convergence/echo tests do not include an explicitly live/end-to-end acceptance criterion that exercises the real send boundary (`issue.update(fields=…)` for DC, the acli encode at `acli.py:205`/`acli_cli_ops.py:369` for Cloud). The DC AC asserts `issue.update(fields=…)` receives rendered wiki, but it is unstated whether the suite drives the real boundary or an offline substitute that could go green without the defaulted path running as in production.

findings.suggested_fix: State whether the convergence tests drive the real send boundary; if they use a substitute, add a live/integration AC (or name the deferred ticket) proving the rendered wire reaches acli/issue.update as in production.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State precisely what re-push `rich_sha` prevents that origin-gating (`local != baseline`) and the once-only re-emit compare do not already prevent — or drop it and gate re-render purely on the existing baseline diff.
evidence: Plan: 'store a change-gated rich_sha = sha256(rendered_wire)[:16] ... so a re-render is only pushed when the wire actually changed. The compare stays comparison-only and never writes back.'
Plan already asserts the emit is origin-gated: 'a description update fires only when local differs from baseline'
Plan already asserts once-only convergence: 'an already-synced body re-emits exactly once ... then converges (the existing once-only re-emit mechanism)'
binding_store.py:105 _BASELINE_FIELDS and outbound_field_diff.py:273-293 already provide the local-vs-baseline-vs-remote gate the plan relies on
findings.finding: The new inline `rich_sha` is a third emission gate whose necessity is under-justified: the plan already states outbound description emit is gated by origin-gating (`local != baseline`) AND the once-only re-emit compare, both of which already bound convergence. The plan justifies rich_sha's SIZING (0.07 KB vs. the rejected per-pass timestamp) but not what re-push it prevents that the existing baseline-diff + compare do not.
findings.location: Plan §'Origin-gating so Jira-native constructs survive (AC5)' / §Scope (binding_store.py); AC 'The rich layer stores a change-gated inline 8-byte rich_sha'
scenarios: A no-op pass where local==baseline: origin-gating already emits nothing, so rich_sha adds no observable suppression.
A rebar-originated change: local!=baseline fires the emit; unclear whether rich_sha would suppress a genuine change or is redundant with the compare.
